newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols drift after PPI.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols drift after PPI.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options ended the day roughly flat after dipping on the morning release of May producer price data.
A 0.3 percent decline in both core and overall U.S. wholesale prices sent underlying September futures soaring to a new 3-1/2-month high.
September bond volatility opened at about 8.4 percent, fell 0.1 percentage point after the producer price index was reported, and finished the session back around 8.4 percent, floor traders said.

The subdued volatility is predictive of the summer doldrums, a period of quiet range trade that market participants associate with July and August but in reality often gets under way in June, said Alex Saitta, technical analyst for Salomon Brothers Inc.

Saitta forecast September volatility could slump to 7.5 percent by mid-July, once the June employment number and the July 1-2 Federal Open Market Committee meeting are out of the way. That would bring it close to the all-time low for front-month bond implied volatility of 7.1 percent, he said.

Bond options activity was brisk early, tapering off as the session wore on, floor traders said. Light profit-taking was seen in the July 111-00 calls, as traders locked in some gains from the two-day rally.

One trading firm bought 2,000 July 112-00 calls, and a dealer firm sold 5,000 July 109-00/110-00/111-00 butterfly put spreads, floor sources said. The transaction involves selling the 109-00 and 111-00 puts 5,000 times each while buying double the amount the amount of 110-00 puts.

August bond options begin trading in the front-month position on Sunday evening, replacing July in that spot. Floor traders predicted volatility in August serial options would open at about 8.4 percent based on Monday's date.

In Eurodollars, September volatility rose 0.5 point to 8.5 percent and December was unchanged at 10.0 percent. Short-dated September volatility, for mid-curve options that expire this year but are priced from 1998 futures, edged down 0.2 point to 14.8 percent.
